ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog is reddish-brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe. It features prominent longitudinal skin ridges on the back and lacks the enlarged outer metatarsal tubercle of similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya rufescens* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored "V" or "W" shaped marking on its throat, which is absent in similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya rufescens* inhabits leaf litter and moist soil within evergreen forests and shaded plantations along the Western Ghats, typically at elevations of 300–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the leaf litter and damp soil of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya rufescens* is an oviparous breeder that lays small clutches of 30–50 eggs in shallow water or mud. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malabar Wart Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at low to mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Wart Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched, insect-like chirps or "tink" sounds, typically heard from shallow water bodies in forest habitats.
